question: Before building a shared-mem+futex transport (lever B), what is the CEILING of per-hop kernel-cost reduction vs the current ~7-syscall UDS coordinator RPC hop, and how much of that ceiling requires the transport rewrite vs a cheap guest-side trim?
timing: CLOCK_MONOTONIC per round-trip; medians + IQR over 200k samples

concurrent_load_at_measurement.note: drain validates carrying the box concurrently; single K=1 bench process, 2 threads, no fan-out. Absolute ns are load-sensitive; inter-mode DELTAS at the same pin are same-run/same-load and are the robust signal.

source_scope_pins_for_context.note: Standalone C microbench; does NOT link hermit/reverie. Pins recorded only to anchor the source-scope (ai_docs/2026-08-04-coordinator-roundtrip-reduction-scope.md) that motivated the comparands.

harness_fidelity_caveat: uds_full issues 3 writes (1B+3B header split + payload) vs the real guest's 2 writes (4B header + payload), so uds_full carries ~8 syscalls vs the real ~7 (overcount of 1 write, a few hundred ns). Conclusion is unaffected: the guest-side-trim delta dominates regardless.
